parameters.text:
=Lead data: {{ JSON.stringify($json.lead) }}

Step 1: Use the Supabase Lead Lookup tool to check whether this lead already exists in the CRM.
Step 2: Use the check_purchase_history tool to see whether this person has bought a vehicle from us before (a returning/VIP customer).
Step 3: Score the lead from 1-100 and classify intent as HOT, WARM or COLD.
  - If check_purchase_history returns ANY prior purchase, this is a RETURNING VIP CUSTOMER: score 90-100 and intent HOT, regardless of how casual the new enquiry sounds.
  - Otherwise: HOT = ready to buy now, specific vehicle, clear budget or urgent language; WARM = genuine interest but no urgency/budget; COLD = just browsing, no budget, no timeline.
Step 4: If the customer states a budget anywhere in their message, report it as budget_aed: a plain number in AED, so 600000 - not "600k", not "AED 600,000", no commas, no currency. If they state no budget at all, use null. Do not guess or infer a budget from the vehicle they asked about.
Step 5: Return your decision.

Do NOT try to save the lead. Persisting it to the CRM is handled downstream by the workflow itself, deterministically, from the decision you return -- so the accuracy of your score, intent and budget_aed is what actually gets written.

Both lookup tools are pre-filtered to this exact lead; call them with no arguments and read the result.

Return ONLY a raw JSON object and nothing else. No markdown, no code fences, no commentary.
Schema: {"score": 95, "intent": "HOT", "reason": "one short sentence", "vip": true, "budget_aed": 600000}

options.systemMessage: You are NEXUS AI, an expert lead scoring agent for a premium car dealership in the UAE. You evaluate inbound leads, check whether they are returning customers, persist them to the CRM, and classify them so the router can dispatch them correctly. Returning customers are extremely valuable and must always be routed as HOT.

nodes.notes: Make.com and Zapier are empty -- every workflow was migrated into n8n -- so nothing external POSTs the webhook any more. This is how the rest of the system reaches the Router now: in-process, no HTTP, no token.

nodes.name: Verify JWT
nodes.notes: Public webhook branch only. A rejected token arrives as data, not as a failed node.

nodes.name: HOT: Already In A Live Chat?
nodes.notes: TRUE = the person is already mid-conversation on WhatsApp; sending canned outreach on top of the reply they just received would be a duplicate message, so that branch is skipped deliberately (not dropped). FALSE = a genuinely new contact, send the outreach.

nodes.name: WARM: Already In A Live Chat?
nodes.notes: TRUE = the person is already mid-conversation on WhatsApp; sending canned outreach on top of the reply they just received would be a duplicate message, so that branch is skipped deliberately (not dropped). FALSE = a genuinely new contact, send the outreach.

nodes.name: Persist Lead (deterministic)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify(Object.assign({ name: $json.lead.name || 'Unknown', email: $json.lead.email || ('+' + String($json.lead.phone || '').replace(/[^0-9]/g,'') + '@whatsapp.lead'), phone: $json.lead.phone, vehicle_interest: $json.lead.vehicle_interest, source: 'nexus-master-router', scoring_state: 'PENDING' }, (Number($json.lead.budget_aed) > 0) ? { budget_aed: Number($json.lead.budget_aed) } : {}, $json.lead.tenant_id ? { tenant_id: $json.lead.tenant_id } : {})) }}

nodes.notes: Added 29 Aug 2026. The lead row must not depend on the model choosing to call a tool - on exec 6253 it simply did not, and the run still audited SUCCESS. Values are bound from Parse AI Decision's item, not from $fromAI.

nodes.name: Update Lead Scoring (PATCH)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify(Object.assign({ ai_score: $json.ai_decision.score, status: $json.ai_decision.intent, scoring_state: 'SCORED', scored_at: new Date().toISOString(), score_source: $json.ai_decision.score_source || 'AI_SCORE_UNKNOWN' }, ($json.ai_decision.score_source === 'RULES') ? { rules_score: $json.ai_decision.rules_score } : { ai_score_raw: ($json.ai_decision.ai_score_raw === undefined ? null : $json.ai_decision.ai_score_raw), ai_intent_raw: ($json.ai_decision.ai_intent_raw === undefined ? null : $json.ai_decision.ai_intent_raw) })) }}

nodes.notes: Added 20 Sep 2026 (NX1002). Second half of persist-first/score-later: 'Persist Lead (deterministic)' already wrote this row as PENDING right after 'Validate & Enrich Input'. This PATCHes the SAME row (same natural key: tenant_id + the same email/synthetic-whatsapp-email derivation Persist Lead uses) to SCORED now that 'Parse AI Decision' has a real ai_decision. Runs in parallel with 'Intent Switch' so a PATCH failure here can never delay or block Slack/ERP/WhatsApp routing. onError=continueRegularOutput: a failure to mark SCORED must not fail the execution -- the row just stays PENDING and the hourly rescore sweep (NEW_rescore_pending_leads) picks it up and finishes the job later; it is idempotent (nexus_record_lead_scoring_result's `scoring_state <> 'SCORED'` guard).

activeVersion.name: Restore ADR-003/NX920 provenance logic in Parse AI Decision
activeVersion.description: Live Parse AI Decision (3517 bytes) lacked the ADR-003/NX920 scoring-provenance logic that exists on origin/main (5893 bytes) -- decoder babble could score a buying lead 0, an empty {} model response was indistinguishable from a genuine WARM/50, partial JSON was trusted, and fenced JSON wasn't recognised. Replaced with main's version, keeping the RULES short-circuit the live version separately gained today (Rule-Based Lead Scorer output with score_source==='RULES' passes through unparsed). Verified 18/18 against ops/scoring/parse-ai-decision.test.js on a local copy before applying.
